content.overview: Harvest-stage deviations should be contained while the affected scope is defined. A sanitation miss, identity uncertainty, environmental delay or suspect material does not automatically prove the entire lot failed, but it cannot be ignored.

vocabulary.definition: Material, time period, location or process plausibly influenced by the deviation.
Controlled status that prevents normal movement or release while evidence and disposition remain unresolved.
Immediate action used to limit further impact while investigation continues.

sections.title: Record facts before theories
sections.body: Capture time, location, material IDs, observed condition and immediate action before deciding cause or final disposition.

sections.title: Use genealogy to define scope
sections.body: Trace lot splits, locations and handling history to identify which material plausibly shared the event.

sections.title: Consequence follows evidence
sections.body: Duration, product condition, later measurements and process knowledge determine whether the event is minor, requires additional evaluation or supports hold/disposition.

workedExamples: A missed sanitation step on one tote line can justify containment of connected material while the event is investigated without automatically placing unrelated lots on indefinite hold.
commonMistakes: Placing the whole facility on hold without evidence.
Releasing affected material because it looks normal.
content.practicalApplication: Complete a harvest deviation record with event facts, immediate containment, affected scope, evidence gaps and escalation owner.
content.summary: Harvest deviations require fast containment and careful scope, not premature certainty.
